messages:
alex: seeing a sudden spike of 429s for org 2542 starting ~1844009800, ~10k 429s/min. dashboards show normal traffic but enormous client-side retries. snippet from proxy logs:
```
2026-03-18T12:10:04Z [proxy] org=2542 key=sk-live-... status=429 reason=rate_limited limit=300 unit=second
2026-03-18T12:10:05Z [proxy] org=2542 key=sk-live-... status=429 reason=rate_limited limit=300 unit=second
```
maya: any config changes recently? product console rollouts? :eyes:
alex: yep, console team pushed a quota backfill and new UI defaults ~1844009600. suspects: unit normalization. backfill used `unit: minute` instead of `second` for migrated orgs.
joel: checking config service now, pulling policy for org 2542...
joel: confirmed policy in db: `{
  "org_id": 2542,
  "limit": 300,
  "unit": "minute",
  "burst": 2
}`
alex: enforcement expects `unit` to be one of `second|minute` but implementation divides bucket tokens assuming `unit=second`. so `limit=300` interpreted as 300/sec => 18k/min. enforcement's preflight also applies `burst` multiplier leading to huge short-term throttling behavior when mismatch occurs.
emily: so console/ backfill wrote minute-based configs, enforcement treated them as seconds => paradoxically we got both over- and under-throttling? can you explain the symptom chain?
joel: enforcement does token refill at per-second resolution. if DB says `minute`, but enforcement doesn't convert, it refills 300 tokens every second (incorrectly). That causes quick token exhaustion due to per-request consume semantics and then a tight 429 loop with clients retrying. basically weird oscillation where bursts hit hard then full throttling.
sre-oncall: can we hotfix by normalizing at the read layer (divide by 60 when unit==minute) and roll that immediately?
maya: yes, but we need to be careful: some orgs legitimately use minute granularity for low-rate long-window policies. patch should be defensive.
alex: proposed hotfix: enforcement read path applies conversion table: `{ minute -> per-second = ceil(limit/60) }` and preserve burst semantics. quick patch accepted?
joel: pushing small patch to internal limiter service now. command: 
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/limiter -- curl -sS -XPOST http://localhost:8080/internal/patch -d '{"convert_minute_unit":true}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
infra-bot: deploy started: limiter-v2.1.9 -> limiter-v2.1.10 by joel at 1844010102
sre-oncall: applied patch, tailing logs... 429 rate for org 2542 dropping from 10k/min -> 200/min in ~90s. looks stable.
emily: can we run a reconciliation job to re-evaluate policies created during the backfill window and add a `unit` validation flag in the console?
maya: yes. followups: 1) rollback backfill script to avoid re-writing unit, 2) add server-side validation on policy create/update that rejects ambiguous units, 3) add metric `policy_unit_mismatch_count` + alert if >5 in 15m, 4) run a migration to convert all `minute` policies to explicit per-second equivalents with annotation.
alex: adding postmortem items to the incident doc. root cause: console backfill used different unit semantics than enforcement; missing integration test and no schema validation in console API.
joel: also add a canary test: when migrating N orgs, sample 5% and run on canary enforcement cluster to detect semantic mismatches.
emily: who will own the migration? suggest infra + product-ops to coordinate. i'll take product-ops side.
sre-oncall: closing incident once recon job finished and alert suppressed. will reopen if mismatch metric spikes.
infra-bot: deploy finished: limiter-v2.1.10 -> success at 1844010185
alex: thanks all :heart: logging followup PRs + migration ticket in #eng-platform. closing thread in 30m unless new errors pop up
